findings.title: KeyError on integration without sender metadata crashes install
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is present, and older/existing Integration rows have no sender key. For those rows this line raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed error page, breaking reinstall/re-link flows.

findings.title: Unhandled token-exchange failure returns 500 instead of error page
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen for the GitHub access_token exchange outside any try/except; only the body parsing is wrapped. Network errors, non-2xx responses, or rate limiting from GitHub will raise and produce a 500. The PR description says a failure to generate an access_token (wrong/reused code) should show the integration-failed page, but that only happens if the endpoint returns a parseable body without access_token.

findings.title: Unhandled get_user_info failure returns 500 instead of error page
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) with no error handling and only checks for missing login key. Any ApiError, auth error, or network failure raised while calling GET /user propagates as an unhandled exception and 500s, instead of returning the intended Invalid installation request error page.

findings.title: Query-param installation_id overrides bound pipeline state
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")) and then re-binds it, so an attacker/crafted OAuth callback URL with ?code=&state=<valid>&installation_id=<other> replaces the installation_id bound in OAuthLoginView before the github_authenticated_user vs sender check. The validated user is then compared against a different installation than the one the pipeline started with, weakening the user-mismatch security check the PR is adding.

findings.title: installation_not_found test no longer exercises 404 path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/<id> to 404 but then drives the second step with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature. The pipeline therefore fails at the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView and never reaches build_integration/get_installation_info. The test asserts Invalid installation request but no longer proves the 404 installation-not-found branch returns a clean error page.
